name: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment
title: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment

claim.quote: The deficit is interpreted as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance.

summary.plain: Double Chooz's detector, 1.05 kilometres from the Chooz reactors in France, saw fewer reactor antineutrinos than expected if the mixing angle θ13 were zero: 8,249 events against 8,937 expected. The collaboration interprets the deficit as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance.
summary.technical: In 227.93 live days (33.71 GW-ton-years exposure), Double Chooz observed 8,249 candidate events versus an expectation of 8,937 for theta_13 = 0. A rate-plus-spectral-shape analysis gives sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.109±0.030(stat)±0.025(syst), excluding the no-oscillation hypothesis at 99.8% CL (2.9σ).

why_it_matters.value: Double Chooz's rate-plus-spectral-shape analysis gives sin²2θ13 = 0.109 ± 0.030(stat) ± 0.025(syst), and the data exclude the no-oscillation hypothesis at 99.8% CL (2.9σ); the collaboration words this as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance, not as an observation.
